title: All Changes May Have Invariant Principles: Improving Ever-Shifting Harmful Meme Detection via Design Concept Reproduction
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the ability of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to detect harmful memes. As part of its taxonomy, 'Religion' is categorized as a macro-type, and the framework evaluates the detection of religious hate, stereotyping, blasphemy, mockery of doctrine, and the misuse of religious symbols (such as Islamic and Buddhist symbols) within memes.
findings: While the paper does not isolate quantitative performance metrics exclusively for religious memes, it demonstrates that its proposed framework (REPMD) successfully improves the detection of ever-shifting harmful memes—which includes religious stereotyping, blasphemy, and symbol misuse. By leveraging Design Concept Graphs (DCG) to understand the underlying malicious intent and invariant principles of the meme creator, the model achieves an overall 81.1% accuracy, outperforming baseline MLLMs.
